data.title: Pennsylvania Benefits Office Supervisor Allegedly Trades Stolen EBT Cards for Crack Cocaine, Drains $20,558 in Food Aid
data.description:
A Pennsylvania county assistance office supervisor is accused of stealing food benefits meant for low-income families and trading some of the cards for crack cocaine.

The Lehigh County District Attorney’s Office says Sheila McDonald, 46, allegedly took more than $20,000 in benefits and swapped them for drugs and cash or used them at area stores, reports WFMZ.

McDonald started at the Lehigh County Assistance Office in January of 2024 and was assigned as its “EBT Coordinator,” the person in charge of securing the Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) cards the office created and mailed out.

That job gave her access to Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) recipients’ personal information, including dates of birth and Social Security numbers.

In November of 2025, the office alerted Pennsylvania’s Office of State Inspector General that a mailed EBT card never reached its owner, even though four unauthorized transactions had been made on it.

Prosecutors allege McDonald used the recipient’s date of birth and the last four digits of their Social Security number to activate the card.

Surveillance video allegedly showed her withdrawing $20 in cash with the card and making purchases at a convenience store and a grocery store.

Investigators also allege that the card was activated through a cell phone number McDonald used, and that the same number was used to activate or check the balance on other EBT cards.

A man told investigators that McDonald often gave him EBT cards, along with the PINs, instead of cash to buy crack cocaine.

Authorities accuse McDonald of activating 48 EBT cards and using them more than 270 times, taking $20,558.61 in total.

She faces felony counts of theft by unlawful taking, theft by deception, access device fraud, criminal conspiracy and receiving stolen property.

McDonald is in custody but has not yet been arraigned.

The Pennsylvania Department of Human Services has suspended her, cut off her access to all systems and issued replacement EBT cards to affected households.

data.title: California-Based Heart Monitor Maker Breached, Affecting 8,179,772 People – Names, Insurance Numbers, Birth Dates and More at Risk
data.description:
A California-based heart monitor maker is warning more than eight million people that hackers stole their personal and health information.

iRhythm Holdings says unauthorized individuals accessed and downloaded data from certain third-party-hosted business applications between June 3rd and June 8th.

The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) breach portal now lists 8,179,772 people as impacted.

The stolen data includes patient names, addresses, email addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth, iRhythm account numbers, device serial numbers, insurance numbers and dates of service.

“On or around June 8, 2026, iRhythm detected unauthorized access in certain third-party-hosted business applications. Upon detecting the unauthorized access, we promptly implemented our incident response plan. As part of our investigation, we have been working very closely with external cybersecurity professionals experienced in handling these types of incidents. After completing our forensic investigation, we learned certain data we store was accessed and downloaded by unauthorized individuals between June 3 and June 8, 2026.”

iRhythm began notifying impacted people on October 2nd.

Says iRhythm,

“iRhythm has no evidence that any personal information has been or will be used to commit identity theft.”

The company is encouraging those affected to place a fraud alert or security freeze on their credit files and get free credit reports.

iRhythm says its medical devices, clinical systems and patient safety were not affected and that it does not store payment card or financial account information.

The Daily Hodl reported earlier this month that state filings showed more than 368,000 people impacted in Texas and South Carolina.

The San Francisco company is best known for its Zio wearable heart monitor.

data.title: Bank of America Handing $2,000,000 to Customers Whose Unauthorized Debit Card and ATM Disputes Were Denied
data.description:
Bank of America is paying $2 million to settle claims that it wrongly turned down customers who reported unauthorized debit card and ATM transactions.

The class action lawsuit, Dennie et al. v. Bank of America, N.A., alleges the bank violated the Electronic Fund Transfer Act (EFTA) by improperly denying those disputes and failing to properly explain the denials, the official settlement website says.

The settlement covers anyone whose dispute over an unauthorized debit card or ATM transaction was denied by Bank of America from May 6th, 2023, through July 14th, 2026.

Class members who file a valid claim get an equal share of the fund after fees and costs are taken out.

Class counsel is asking the court for $666,666.67 in attorneys’ fees, or one-third of the fund, on top of reasonable costs and expenses.

Bank of America, one of the largest banks in the US, will pay current account holders with a credit to their account, while former account holders will get a check.

The deal only releases claims for statutory damages under the EFTA, not claims for the money people actually lost.

Bank of America has also agreed to change the written explanation it sends customers whose unauthorized debit card and ATM claims are denied.

Says the settlement website,

“Bank of America denies that it did anything wrong, but it agreed to the Settlement to avoid the uncertainties and expenses associated with continuing the case.”

Claims must be filed by December 11th using the ID on the postcard or email notice that the class members received.

The final approval hearing is set for January 4th, 2027.

The Daily Hodl first covered the lawsuit when it was filed in May of 2024.

data.title: South Carolina Woman Drains $37,645 From Four West Virginia Bank Accounts Using Stolen Identities and Forged Signatures
data.description:
A South Carolina woman is headed to prison after using other people’s identities to pull more than $37,000 out of four West Virginia bank accounts that were not hers.

Della Palestino, 60, of Lexington, South Carolina, was sentenced to two years in prison and one year of supervised release for aggravated identity theft, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of West Virginia says.

She was also ordered to pay $47,010 in restitution for the aggravated identity theft.

Prosecutors say Palestino went to four financial institutions in southern West Virginia and used a different person’s personal information each time, including a forged signature, to get into that person’s bank account without permission.

She withdrew $21,920 in Spencer, $4,200 in Charleston and $9,400 in Gilbert in September of 2024, along with $2,125 in Huntington.

The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of West Virginia says,

“As part of her guilty plea, Palestino admitted that she conducted all four fraudulent transactions and withdrew a total of $37,645 from the bank accounts of the four individuals. Palestino further admitted that she used a counterfeit passport card during one of the fraudulent withdrawals.”

The case was investigated by the U.S. Department of State’s Diplomatic Security Service, the West Virginia State Police and police departments in Huntington, Charleston and Gilbert.

data.title: Up to $8,500 per Person To Be Handed Out by Ivy League University After Data Breach That Impacted 2,973,631 People
data.description:
Nearly three million people may qualify for payments of up to $8,500 each under a data breach settlement tied to a major university cyberattack.

Columbia University has agreed to pay $16,125,000 to settle a class action lawsuit over the May of 2025 attack on its network, the settlement website says.

The case is In re Columbia University Data Breach Litigation in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York.

The class covers U.S. residents whose private information was compromised in the attack and who were sent a notice about it. Columbia estimates there are 2,973,631 class members.

The stolen data included Social Security numbers, financial details, medical information and academic histories.

Class members with documents showing losses from the attack can get reimbursed up to $8,500. Others can instead choose an alternative cash payment, which will be a share of what is left in the fund after attorneys’ fees, administration costs and other expenses are paid.

Everyone who files can also get two years of free three-bureau credit monitoring, dark web monitoring, up to $1 million in identity theft insurance and identity recovery services.

Columbia denies any wrongdoing but has committed to keep added security measures in place for three years.

The deadline to file a claim is January 21st, 2027. The deadline to opt out or object is December 22nd, 2026.

A final approval hearing is set for February 23rd, 2027.

The Daily Hodl previously reported on the breach in August of 2025.

data.title: AI-Powered Bank Scam Drains $423,114 From 170 Victims in Just Three Weeks: Report
data.description:
Police in the Netherlands have arrested two men suspected of running a new kind of bank scam that used AI-generated phone calls to drain about €380,000 (approximately $423,114) from 170 victims in just three weeks.

The Rotterdam police cybercrime team says the men, a 23-year-old from Vaassen and a 25-year-old from Ede, were taken into custody on October 6th.

Police say the 23-year-old is suspected of building the technology behind the fraud and directing others in the group, while the 25-year-old is suspected of coordinating the operation.

Victims got a phone call with a recorded message warning of suspicious activity on their bank account.

The scammers allegedly used AI to make dozens of recordings with different voices, banks, companies and scenarios.

Victims who pressed 1 were connected to a fake bank employee, who followed a script and pushed them to act fast to block their bank card.

They were told to download an app and hold their bank card against their phone.

Police say the app sent data from the card’s contactless chip to an app used by an accomplice waiting at an ATM or payment terminal, who could then withdraw thousands of euros without the victim knowing.

Victims came from all over the Netherlands and ranged in age, including dozens in their twenties and thirties.

The investigation began in mid-September, when Dutch banks flagged the new method through the Electronic Crimes Task Force, a partnership of banks, police and prosecutors.

Police have taken the servers behind the scheme offline and seized the suspects’ phones and laptops.

A Rotterdam court ruled on October 20th that both men must stay in custody for at least another 90 days while the case moves forward.

Says Ruben van Well of the Rotterdam cybercrime team, in remarks translated from Dutch,

“No more scammer at the door, but a convincing caller who comes across as incredibly professional. We had not come across that technical method before…

Your bank will never ask you to download an app, hold your bank card against your phone or give your PIN code. Be alert and hang up if the conversation doesn’t feel right.”

data.title: JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo and Goldman Sachs Among 33 Listed Companies Blocking Tokenized Versions of Their Stock on a Crypto Exchange-Fronted Joint Venture
data.description:
Seven more major companies are blocking tokenized versions of their shares from a planned 24/7 crypto trading venue, bringing the total number of objectors to 33.

JPMorgan Chase, Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Coca-Cola, Applied Materials, Adobe, Dell Technologies and Sandisk now appear on a revised public notice dated October 27th from OKXICE, the joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and New York Stock Exchange parent Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), according to a filing.

The objection list stood at 26 companies in the version dated one day earlier.

The earlier objectors include Microsoft, Alphabet, Goldman Sachs, Oracle, IBM and Intel.

JPMorgan is now the third bank on the list, joining Goldman Sachs and Wells Fargo.

All seven new objectors were among the 63 tickers OKXICE listed for tokenized trading in its first notice, dated October 4th.

The new notice does not give a reason for any of the objections, and it still does not give a launch date for the venue.

Under the SEC’s exemption for tokenized stock venues, a venue must notify a company before trading a token of its stock that was created by an unaffiliated third party.

A written objection from the company within 30 calendar days keeps the token off the venue.

The count has climbed with each new notice, from nine on October 15th to 16 on October 19th and 22 on October 23rd.

The notice also keeps its earlier risk warnings, including one about upgrades to the venue’s smart contracts.

Says the notice,

“[Changes] take effect without a timelock, so TSV Participants may receive no advance notice of an upgrade.”

As Daily Hodl previously reported, OKXICE first notified the SEC earlier this month of its plans to offer round-the-clock trading of tokenized versions of more than 60 major US stocks.

data.title: $7,500 Abruptly Drained From a Florida Couple’s Wells Fargo Account After Criminals Impersonating Her Bank Call Her
data.description:
Scammers posing as Wells Fargo’s fraud department have taken more than $7,500 from a couple after convincing them to read back verification codes sent to their phone.

Carmen Evans says the caller ID on her phone showed Wells Fargo, and the man on the line, who called himself Michael, told her there were questionable transactions on her account, reports WKMG News 6.

The caller mentioned purchases at Sam’s Club and Walmart that the Orlando, Florida resident recognized, then brought up a $3,000 charge she says she never made.

Says Evans,

“I did not have to give him my name. The only thing he asked me at that point was, ‘You’re going to be getting some text with the code. Just make sure you repeat the code to me.’”

After she shared the codes, Evans says she could no longer get into her bank accounts.

She and her husband, William, went to a Wells Fargo branch, where William says an employee told them there was activity in their accounts while they were standing there.

The couple says money was shifted between their accounts and then sent out through Cash App using Carmen’s linked Wells Fargo debit card, transfers she says she did not make.

The losses included about $3,000 in savings, plus her Social Security payment and paychecks from her part-time job.

“They took stuff that we needed, and we had to turn around and take loans to cover bills.”

With rent and a car payment due, the couple also had to ask their children for help.

Says William,

“It was hard to go to our children just to say, ‘Well, this happened. And now we don’t have any money.’”

Evans says she disputed the transactions but has not been able to get the money back.

She has since deleted Cash App, and the couple says they are moving their banking elsewhere.

The American Bankers Association says banks will not call customers and ask for their one-time login codes.

data.title: $5,000,000,000 Abruptly Exits Binance Wallets As Founder Warns Exchange ‘May Have Been Hacked’
data.description:
Binance is investigating reports of a major hack amid a series of massive crypto transfers.

The company says it has not confirmed any impact to user funds at this stage, while its founder Changpeng Zhao warns the exchange appears to have been hacked.

“User funds are safe! It does look like a hack on Binance.

Appreciate the quick freeze from Tether (~$971m) and Circle (~$823m). I don’t manage Binance (.com) anymore, but as a shareholder, I expect all user funds will be fully covered.”

At time of publishing, it appears more than $5 billion in crypto on three blockchains has been drained.

Data from Etherscan shows the first Ethereum transaction sent 167,464 ETH plus 63 token transfers to a new address.

The total stands at around $3.51 billion on Ethereum, $1.44 billion in Bitcoin and $630 million on Tron.

Binance itself says it is still investigating.

“Our teams are aware of reports of a potential security issue and are actively investigating.

At this stage, we have not confirmed any impact to user funds.

Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information.

Users should remain cautious of scams and should not trust unofficial links, messages, or requests for account information.”

data.title: Nigerian National Extradited from Africa, Arraigned in Georgia on $100,000,000 Identity Theft Tax Scheme
data.description:
Federal prosecutors have arraigned a Nigerian national on multiple fraud and identity theft charges after his extradition from Benin, West Africa, in a scheme that targeted the US tax system.

Akinade Adedeji Raheem, 43, of Nigeria was ordered detained pending further proceedings in Atlanta following his arraignment on conspiracy to commit wire and mail fraud, conspiracy to commit money laundering, 14 counts of access device fraud and 14 counts of aggravated identity theft, says the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Georgia.

Raheem and Abayomi Quadri Eletu, a resident of the United Kingdom and Nigeria, allegedly stole accountant and taxpayer data to submit more than 300 false returns between 2018 and 2023, claiming over $100 million in refunds from the Internal Revenue Service (IRS).

“Raheem, Eletu, and others allegedly obtained sensitive identifying information for tax professionals and taxpayers, including names, addresses, and Social Security numbers, by creating online accounts with the IRS and requesting private taxpayer information. Using the personal identifying information of others, Raheem, Eletu, and their co-conspirators allegedly filed tax returns claiming fraudulent refunds…”

The proceeds were allegedly laundered through prepaid debit cards and purchases of used cars shipped to Nigeria, designer clothes and other items.

Says US Attorney Theodore S. Hertzberg,

“Raheem and his co-conspirators allegedly obtained hundreds of stolen identities, filed fraudulent tax returns using that information, and laundered the proceeds through prepaid debit cards and purchases of used cars that were shipped to Nigeria and other location. The scope of the alleged fraud is staggering. Thanks to the dedication of the prosecution team and our law enforcement partners around the world, Raheem has been extradited to the United States, and his arrest confirms again that no alleged criminal can escape the reach of American justice.”

Raheem faces maximum penalties of 20 years in prison for conspiracy to commit mail and wire fraud, 20 years for money laundering, 10 years for access device fraud, and a mandatory two-year sentence for aggravated identity theft.
